newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower under Wall Street pressure.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower under Wall Street pressure.

text.p: A feeble early Wall Street put Swiss shares under pressure in late trade and the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell below the important level of 3,800 points.
Shares of watchmaker SMH fell 2.9 percent or 25 Swiss francs to 822 francs on a negative study of the Smart Car joint venture with Mercedes.
Standard & Poor's Marketscope said the SMH share price did not reflect greater risks than generally recognised from the Smart Car, due to be launched in early 1998.
The SMI gave up 0.28 percent, or 10.6 points, to 3,797.3.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 0.2 percent, or 4.85 points, to 2,430.54 points.
"The market just could not continue to soar as fast as it did in the past few days", one trader said, adding the SMI may fall as low as 3,750 before picking up again.
"But the fundamentals remain excellent", he said.
Investors concentrated on Friday's U.S. PPI data, which was expected to move the market again, dealers said. Today's U.S. jobless data pressured U.S. bonds and early Wall Street trade.
Heavily-traded Roche certificates slid 50 francs to 9,530.
UBS bearer shares bucked the trend, adding seven francs to 1,250. Speculation about imminent restructuring moves may have had a positive effect, on trader noted.

CS Holding fell 0.6 percent to 128 francs. Friday's extraordinary shareholder meeting was only scheduled to approve a name change to Credit Suisse Group, dealers said. There had been speculation earlier that CS would announce the sale of its major stake in power and building controls group Electrowatt.
ABB added one franc to 1,557. News that Goran Lindahl was to succeed Percy Barnevik as CEO had little effect, dealers said.
Alusuisse ended unchanged at 939 after Wednesday's losses.
Swissair added nine franc, help by a call option.
Second-tier insurer Berner Holding jumped 3.8 percent.
